subject.title: [Bug][iOS] chat.history reconciliation duplicates and reorders replies after tool runs

question: Do the current-main request-ID and mutation-generation guards sufficiently resolve this release trace, or must the exact delayed-history sequence be reproduced on an iOS build before implementation work is promoted?
rationale: Source now contains directly relevant post-release protection, but it does not prove the reported concurrent history burst, tool-row projection, and final chronology together; accepting or rejecting the existing evidence requires native-chat owner judgment.

options.title: Require exact replay
options.body: Keep the issue open until a deterministic delayed-response test and an iOS run confirm that current main remains deduplicated and ordered.

options.title: Accept source protection
options.body: Treat the current request-generation guards as sufficient only after identifying their fix commit and confirming the issue's sequence is covered by existing tests.

options.title: Promote immediate repair
options.body: Proceed directly with single-flight history scheduling and stronger sequence-based projection if owners consider the release trace sufficient without another live reproduction.

recommendation.title: Require exact replay
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a deterministic delayed-response test and an iOS run confirm that current main remains deduplicated and ordered.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor most recently changed and tested the exact shared native-chat reconciliation boundary.
